subject: Reserved capacity hedge + SKU oversubscription plan for Velox AI
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@velox.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-20T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity question — model mix and memory headroom

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the call earlier. We ran a quick pass on our production mix and attached a CSV with 1 week of sampled traffic (velox_workload_samples.csv). Short version: we have three model classes in prod — long-context RAG generation (~18% of requests, median context 32k tokens), standard chat/assistant (~62%), and high-volume embeddings (~20%).

We're evaluating a 12-month reserved commitment and want Redwood's recommendation for the SKU split. Key asks from our side:
- Cost-optimal set of SKUs to reserve (H100 vs A100 vs L4) given the above mix
- How to size headroom for token spikes and KV cache pressure for the RAG flows
- A fallback/oversubscription policy (reserve vs burst) that limits outages but keeps committed costs reasonable

Can you take a first pass and share a recommended reserve/burst split + short rationale? Attachment included.

Cheers,
Samir
Lead SRE, Velox AI

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity question — model mix and memory headroom

Samir — thanks, got the samples. Looping Ben for deal economics and Priya + Irene for ops/quantization constraints. We will draft a short reserve/burst plan and a hedging policy. Expect a first-pass later today.

Quick note to the Velox team: if you have percentile latency SLOs (p95/p99) and tail token distribution for RAG sessions that would help calibrate headroom — otherwise we'll use conservative defaults.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-20T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity question — model mix and memory headroom

Agree we should avoid an all-in H100 reserve — cost will be prohibitive for Velox's volume. Initial commercial view: propose a mixed reserve where Velox commits to a base pool for 70% of baseline steady-state RPS, with burst credits for top 30% traffic. That keeps committed spend predictable while allowing controlled oversubscription.

Ballpark hourly equivalent costs (for modeling only):
- H100 (80GB): ~$15/hr reserved-equivalent unit; best for long-context models where KV cache and >40GB activations are required.
- A100 (40GB): ~$7.5/hr reserved-equivalent unit; good medium trotter for multi-turn chat with medium contexts or for batching throughput.
- L4 (24GB): ~$2.8/hr reserved-equivalent unit; cost-efficient for embeddings and short chat.

We should convert Velox's token mix into equivalent GPU-hours under different split scenarios. Priya — can you compute perf multipliers for their sampled workloads (attach proposed_capacity_matrix.xlsx as template)? Irene — flag any ops/eviction concerns for large KV caches under oversubscription.

-ben
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-21T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity question — model mix and memory headroom

Attaching the capacity matrix draft (proposed_capacity_matrix.xlsx) and a short ops note (fallback_policy.md). Summary of the profiling I ran against Velox samples:

- Long-context RAG (model: huggingface/velox-rag-32k): median sequence length + KV cache usage maps to ~0.9 H100 GPU-hours per 1k requests at Velox's request size; A100 degrades throughput ~2.4x for same latency target because of reduced NVLink/KV bandwidth and lower memory headroom.
- Chat (model: open-chat-medium, 8k windows): ~0.35 A100 GPU-hours per 1k requests; L4 can handle many chat requests but will hit latency and quality regressions for multi-turn when context grows beyond 6k tokens.
- Embeddings (dense, 512-d): best run on L4; measured cost per 1k calls on L4 is ~0.07 L4 GPU-hours.

Recommendations (conservative reserve mix for 12-month commitment):
- Reserve: 8 x H100 (80GB) | 24 x A100 (40GB) | 64 x L4 (24GB)
  Rationale: H100 reserved covers steady long-context baseline and KV cache headroom; A100 handles most chat throughput; L4 for embeddings and short-turn chat to keep unit economics low.
- Burst pool: allow 1.6x burst factor across A100/L4 (pooled burst credits) with automatic routing to cloud burst where Redwood-hosted capacity is available (cost pass-through).
- Oversubscription policy: allocate KV cache pinning for H100 long-context sessions and restrict eviction frequency — fallback to A100 only when sessions can tolerate reduced KV residency (we'll preserve session affinity).

I've included per-day/hour cost and a sensitivity sheet in the XLSX — see 'scenario_B' tab for 20% traffic growth and a 2x tail event. Under scenario_B, recommended reserve cushions p99 latency by ~40% vs a pure A100 reserve.

Priya
Applied ML — Redwood Inference
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@velox.ai>, Lisa Gomez <lgomez@velox.ai>

Date: 2028-08-22T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity question — model mix and memory headroom

Samir / Lisa — attaching the finalized recommendation and an ops playbook (see attachments). TL;DR: we recommend the following 12-month reserved commitment and operational hedge: 

Recommended reserved commitment (initial):
- 8 x H100 (80GB) — dedicated to long-context RAG workers with KV pinning (covers ~75% of steady long-context demand)
- 24 x A100 (40GB) — primary chat/assistant capacity (covers ~70% of chat baseline)
- 64 x L4 (24GB) — embeddings and cost-efficient front-line chat capacity

Operational hedges and policies:
- Burst buffer: allow dynamic burst to shared cloud pool up to 1.6x committed RPS. Burst charges are billed at pass-through rates with a capped monthly overage percentage (negotiable).
- Oversubscription guard: we will oversubscribe L4 up to 1.8x for embeddings (because embeddings are short-lived and cache-friendly), but limit oversubscription on H100 to <1.05x to avoid KV thrash on long-context sessions.
- Fallback chain: H100 -> A100 (degraded latency/throughput but maintains correctness) -> L4 (best-effort for short contexts only). Long-context sessions will be pinned; if a pinned session cannot be scheduled, we queue and surface a graceful degradation response rather than silent truncation.
- Monitoring & alerting: p50/p95/p99 latency, KV eviction rate, active pinned sessions, slot saturation. We'll provide a per-route dashboard and weekly capacity burn report.

Next steps: Ben will formally update the commercial term sheet with the reserve numbers and our suggested burst cap. Priya/Irene will hand off the detailed scenario calculations and operational runbook. Samir/Lisa — if you can confirm target p99 latency and acceptable monthly overage cap (e.g., 10% vs 20%), we'll finalize the commitment and run a 2-week pilot to validate tail behavior.

Thanks — look forward to moving this forward.

—Michael
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
